**Finding submitted: MISSING (critical) — no Vendor/Contractor indemnity in the Agreement.**

What I found:

- **Section 7 is titled "LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR"** but contains no indemnity text — only a fees-paid liability cap (7(a)), a consequential-damages waiver (7(b)) and an attorneys'-fee waiver (7(c)).
- Document-wide searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "defend" returned **only the Section 7 heading** — there is no indemnity anywhere, in either direction. (The planner's concern about a one-way Customer indemnity turned out to be a heading artefact; nothing operative runs against us either.)
- Section 5(c) provides only a non-infringement **warranty**, which does not carry a duty to defend or fund third-party claims, so it cannot satisfy the rule even at fallback.
- Note also that 7(a) preserves a carve-out for "Contractor's obligations pursuant to Paragraph 9", but Paragraph 9 is now *Independent Contractor* — a vestigial cross-reference suggesting an indemnity was deleted from the draft.

Redline (validated, ok:true): inserted a new **Section 7(d)** after p0037 requiring Contractor to defend and indemnify Company and its affiliates for (i) IP infringement/misappropriation by the Services or Works, (ii) breach of applicable law, (iii) Contractor-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of Confidential Information, and (iv) gross negligence or wilful misconduct — with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and an express carve-out from the Section 7(a)–(c) limitations so the indemnity isn't neutralised by the fees-paid cap and fee waiver. The comment offers the fallback (customary IP exclusions plus procure/modify/replace/refund remedies) as a negotiating path.
